facts.text: Afton once thrived as a railroad town, thanks to the Blue Ridge Tunnel built in the 1850s.
French engineer Claudius Crozet, known as the “Pathfinder of the Blue Ridge,” directed the construction of four mountain tunnels, including the longest in the region.
Afton sits in the foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains, about 20 miles west of Charlottesville.
The town’s historic core includes the mid‑19th‑century villages of Greenwood Depot and Afton, plus early‑20th‑century African‑American communities of New Town and Free Town.
Afton is home to several craft producers, including Hazy Mountain Vineyards & Brewery, Silverback Distillery, Veritas Vineyard and Winery, Blue Mountain Brewery, and Cardinal Point Vineyard & Winery.
Scott Castle, a 25,000‑square‑foot Tudor‑Gothic mansion built in 1911 by engineer Henry Baskervill and architect John Russell Pope, once hosted a charity auction for local fire services.
